newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's Sadi to run in parliamentary elections.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's Sadi to run in parliamentary elections.

text.p: Algerian former presidential candidate Said Sadi said on Thursday his Rally for Culture and Democracy (RCD) party will run in the troubled North African country's proposed parliamentary elections later this year.
"We decide in favour of the principle of taking part as the country cannot do with a desertion by democratic forces," Sadi told France's Radio Beur-FM.
"However, we must not have any illusion about the new assembly's legislative power. It is restricted," he added.
President Liamine Zeroual met 10 political party leaders earlier this week and proposed May 29 or June 5 this year as tentative dates for the elections.
Authorities scrapped 1992 elections which the Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) was poised to win. More than 60,000 people have died since Moslem rebels took up arms after the polls were cancelled.
Algerian authorities have said only legal political parties will be allowed to run, therefore excluding the FIS which was outlawed after the 1992 polls were cancelled.
Main secular opposition groups stayed away from the talks with Zeroual, saying Algeria needs peace before holding any elections.
The Socialist Forces Front (FFS) has urged authorities since 1992 to open negotiations with the main opposition parties, including the FIS to end the bloodshed before holding elections.
